title: SDK + Control Plane: client helpers and safety gates for progressive model rollouts
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Implement end-to-end support in the control plane and client SDKs for progressive model rollouts. This includes idempotent rollout mutation APIs, scoped rollout tokens for permissioned operations, SDK helpers for deterministic traffic splitting and shadowing, observability hooks that emit evaluation traces used by auto-rollback policies, and a safety gate that prevents rollouts when preconditions fail. Goal is to make canary/A-B/shadow deployments safe, auditable, and reversible without requiring teams to write ad-hoc orchestration code.
background: Customers are increasingly adopting progressive rollouts (canaries, A/B experiments, shadow traffic) to validate model updates. Current flow scatters logic between the Console, server-side scripts and SDKs which causes drift (non-idempotent operations, missing audit trails, and inconsistent routing/telemetry). Several PM tickets requested richer SDK primitives and control-plane guarantees to make these patterns reproducible and safe.
goals: Provide idempotent HTTP API endpoints for creating/updating rollout objects (create-or-reconcile semantics)
Expose SDK client helpers for traffic split calculation, deterministic assignment for A/B, and transparent shadowing
Emit standardized rollout events and evaluation traces consumed by auto-rollback workers
Implement permission-scoped rollout tokens and enforcement hooks in the control plane
Add a pre-flight safety gate to block rollouts that would violate SLOs or security policies
non_goals: Building a full experiment analytics pipeline (this ticket will emit telemetry, analytics team owns aggregation)
Changing existing billing semantics for routed traffic
api_contract: PATCH /v1/rollouts/{id}/adjust - atomic traffic update with optimistic lock header
POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/evaluate - ingest evaluation trace for policy decisions
GET /v1/rollouts/{id}/audit - paginated change log with actor and token type
sdk_surface: RolloutClient.shadowRequest(req, rolloutId) -> forwards a copy with tenant-scoped metadata
RolloutClient.waitForStable(rolloutId, timeout) -> polls evaluation state and returns outcome
acceptance_criteria: Control plane endpoints support idempotent create-or-reconcile semantics and accept an Idempotency-Key header
SDK helpers deterministically assign variants across language SDKs (JS/Python/Go) with same seed algorithm
Rollout events and evaluation traces contain required fields: rollout_id, actor, timestamp, delta_metrics, sample_size, request_hash
Auto-rollback worker reads evaluation traces and triggers rollback when configured thresholds (latency/error/regression) are exceeded
Permission model enforces that only principals with rollout:write + project scope can modify rollout traffic allocations
Audit endpoint returns full mutation history including idempotency keys and token types (service, user, safetynet)
E2E test demonstrating canary -> increase -> observe regression -> automatic rollback using staged test harness
tasks: Control plane: implement create-or-reconcile endpoint with idempotency support (ENG backend)
Control plane: add optimistic lock header (+ 409 handling) for PATCH traffic adjustments
SDKs: implement deterministic assignment function parity across JS/Python/Go
SDKs: add shadowRequest helper that preserves tenant metadata and injects rollout headers
Observability: define rollout event schema and wire to event bus
Auto-rollback: implement worker that samples evaluation traces, applies rules, and posts rollback command
Authz: rollout tokens with limited scope and TTL; enforce in control plane
Tests: unit tests, integration tests, and an E2E pipeline job that runs against staging
risks: Idempotency semantics may interact poorly with concurrent reconcile loops from multiple clients
Deterministic assignment algorithm must be byte-identical across languages to avoid split-brain routing
Evaluation trace volume could increase costs if not sampled or rate-limited
Permission-scoped tokens need careful UX to avoid teams creating wide-scope tokens that bypass safeguards
implementation_notes: Use RFC 7231 Idempotency-Key header pattern; persist key -> operation mapping for 24 hours
Assignment algorithm: MurmurHash3(user_id + rollout_id + variant_salt) modulo 10000 for percentile splits
Trace schema fields: { rollout_id, step, variant, metric_buckets, sample_count, request_hash, actor_id }
Auto-rollback worker will use rolling windows (5m/30m) with configurable thresholds per rollout
Permission tokens issued by auth service; include token_type label in audit log (service|user|safeguard)
Expose a dry-run flag to simulate traffic split changes without applying them to live routing
blockers: Auth service needs a minor token-scoping extension (ENG-21012). Observability team needs to agree on trace schema and retention policy.
qa_plan: Unit tests for idempotency edge cases (replayed keys, partial failures)
Integration tests that exercise concurrent PATCH and create races
Staging E2E: deploy small canary, inject synthetic traffic, assert evaluation trace emits, then trigger regression and assert auto-rollback
Manual security review of rollout tokens and audit logs
notes: PM asked to keep UI surface minimal for initial launch; Console team will read audit logs and surface staged controls later
We should coordinate with analytics to avoid double-counting shadowed requests for billing
Consider limiting evaluation trace retention to 7 days by default and customizable per-tenant
